quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A simple way to make your motorcycle easier to see is to:

options.text: Ride with a large flag attached to the frame.
Ride on the shoulder whenever possible.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Wear bright, reflective clothing. Use your turn signals and brake light properly. These steps help other drivers see you.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. These signs show rules you must follow. Other signs have different shapes.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should only be done on long trips.
Should be part of your regular scanning routine.
Are not helpful since you cannot change what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your regular scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often. Always check them before changing lanes, stopping at an intersection, or slowing down.

questions.question: Smoothly downshifting on motorcycles:

options.text: Allows the rider to use engine braking.
Should not be done when other vehicles are around.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows the rider to use engine braking.
questions.explanation: Downshifting smoothly lets you use engine braking to slow down. If you engine brake, use your brake lights separately so other drivers know you are slowing down.

questions.question: Common drugs, such as cold tablets:

options.text: Can affect your ability to safely operate your motorcycle.
Usually will not affect your ability to safely operate your motorcycle.
Have no risk to your operating ability.
Are always safe to take before riding because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to safely operate your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, including over-the-counter medicines, can affect your ability to ride safely. Know the side effects of any drug before you ride.

questions.question: Locking your brakes can:
questions.explanation: Locked brakes cause control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and reapply it. If your rear brake locks on good pavement, keep it locked until you stop.

questions.question: To provide the best protection, a helmet should:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: When looking for a protective jacket or pants, you should choose:
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to protect your arms and legs. Leather clothing provides the best protection.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Travel on the shoulder to stay away from other traffic.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes when needed, reduce speed, and avoid sudden moves. Be careful on wet areas, shaded spots, dirt, gravel, and bridges.

questions.question: Which of the following is a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted markings, and metal covers can be slippery. Ride with extra caution on these surfaces.

questions.question: Which surface does NOT have poor traction?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all reduce tire traction. Dry pavement is the safest surface for a motorcycle.

questions.question: As a motorcycle rider, how can you help others see you?
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright clothing, keep your headlight on at all times, and always use your turn signals.

questions.question: What is usually found in the center of a traffic lane?
questions.explanation: Oil and grease from cars drip onto the road and form a strip in the center of each lane. In dry conditions, it is usually still safe for a motorcycle to ride on this strip.

questions.question: What do goggles protect when you are riding?

options.text: Your eyes, but not your face.
Your face, but not your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your eyes, but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. A face shield protects your entire face. Regular eyeglasses do not offer enough protection.

questions.question: What does a face shield do?
questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield gives the best protection for your eyes and face. Eyeglasses or sunglasses are not enough protection. In Vermont, you do not need eye or face protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still recommended.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in daylight. How can you be more visible?
questions.explanation: Since most crashes happen during the day, wear bright clothing while riding, even in daylight.

questions.question: Which item is NOT considered protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing while riding. This includes sturdy pants and jackets that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover your ankles, and sturdy gloves. A stocking cap does not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: When should a rider use their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down or stopping, when stopped at an intersection, when changing lanes, and when turning.

questions.question: How much alcohol does the body eliminate per hour?
questions.explanation: On average, the body can eliminate about one drink per hour.

questions.question: What must you have to carry a passenger on a motorcycle?

options.text: A seat large enough for two riders.
The passenger should not wear protective clothing.
A sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: A seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat designed for two riders. It must have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear that you wear.

questions.question: Shifting into a lower gear has an effect similar to:
questions.explanation: Shifting into a lower gear slows your motorcycle down, similar to using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Move to one side of your lane to allow them to share the lane.

questions.explanation: The safest action is to let the tailgater pass. Change lanes when it is safe and let them go ahead. Speeding up will only make the danger worse.

questions.question: What type of material offers the best protection for motorcyclists?
questions.explanation: Leather provides the best protection for motorcyclists. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs completely when riding.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends a SEE strategy for safe riding. What does "SEE" stand for?
questions.explanation: Good riders use the SEE strategy to make safe decisions while riding. SEE stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
